**Collection:** Abhidhamma

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Tikauddesa* is the third section of the opening schedule or matrix (*mātikā-uddesa*) of the *Puggalapaññatti*, a treatise in the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hirakawa 1990]. In the introductory framework of the *Puggalapaññatti*, the category of persons (*puggala*) is systematically subdivided into numerical groupings ranging from one to ten individuals [Hirakawa 1990]. The *Tikauddesa* presents the matrix of triads—classifications of persons grouped by threes—serving as the index for the detailed expositions found later in the *Tikapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.3) [Hirakawa 1990].

**Sources**

- [Hirakawa 1990] Akira Hirakawa, History of Indian Buddhism: From Śākyamuni to Early Mahāyāna (1990) — Explains the role of the mātikā-uddesa in the Puggalapaññatti and the numerical subdivision of human types from one to ten.
